Page 2 of 15 I. Purpose and scope The Walltopia Preliminary Loads Calculator is a multiplatform tool for selecting and presenting characteristic preliminary loads imposed by artificial climbing structures (ACS) on an existing building structure. It reproduces the approved Walltopia preliminary-load datasets through a guided interface and presents the selected values in tables and technical diagrams. IMPORTANT The calculator is intended for preliminary assessment only. It does not perform final structural design, anchor design, connection verification or code compliance verification. The calculator supports: • Climbing walls with protection points and bouldering walls. • Metric (kN, m) and imperial (lb, ft) unit systems. • Selection of wall height, attachment scheme, column span, overhang and live-load force level. • Characteristic and optional factored values, capacity orientation, 2D diagrams, PDF reports, saved projects and Engineering Support inquiries. Load values shall be reviewed and factored by a qualified structural engineer according to the applicable national standard.

Page 3 of 15 II. Calculator overview The desktop calculator is divided into an input panel on the left and a live results area on the right. Every input selection immediately updates the applicable schemes and calculated values. The same calculation logic is used by the web and mobile clients. The mobile interface reorganises the controls into a vertical workflow and separates Results, Diagram and Notes into readable sections.

Page 4 of 15 III. Worked example III.1. Example 1 - climbing wall, metric units 1. Choose the preferred units Select Metric (kN, m) for characteristic forces in kilonewtons and dimensions in metres. Select Imperial (lb, ft) when the project requires US customary units. 2. Choose the structure type Select Climbing wall for an ACS with protection points or Boulder wall for a structure without protection points. The applicable heights, attachment schemes and load datasets are different.

Page 5 of 15 3. Select the climbing-surface height Choose the nominal height of the climbing surface. Only heights covered by the approved preliminary-load dataset are available. For this worked example select 12 m. 4. Select the attachment scheme The attachment scheme defines the number and elevation of attachment levels along the height of the ACS. Available schemes are filtered automatically after the wall height is selected. For this example select 3 attachment levels: Z1 = 4.0 m, Z2 = 8.0 m and Z3 = 11.5 m.

Page 6 of 15 5. Select column span A A is the span between the existing building columns or frames. The selected span affects the loads reported for the building columns, especially the dead-load components. For this example select A = 6 m. 6. Select overhang X X is the horizontal difference between the bottom and top contours of the climbing surface. Use the representative or most unfavourable overhang in the vicinity of the investigated column or frame. For this example select X = 1 m.

Page 7 of 15 7. Select the live-load force level The force-level control selects the attachment level at which the live load is taken at its local maximum. The concurrent live-load values shown at the other levels belong to the same load situation. Review each available force level separately when identifying the governing action for an existing column or frame. IMPORTANT Do not combine the maximum live -load value from every force -level selection into one simultaneous load case. Use one selected force-level situation at a time with its displayed concurrent values.

Page 8 of 15 IV. Reading the results The results table separates loads on one ACS axis from the loads applied to the existing building column or frame. Symbol Meaning Use R Load on one axis of the ACS Base points and single-axis attachment points L Load on a building column / frame Primary values for assessment of the existing structure DL Dead load Acts on the supporting structure and must be factored LL Live load Climber load case with the selected maximum force level Z0 Vertical component at the base Vertical load at the ACS base X0-X3 Horizontal components Base and attachment-level actions

Page 9 of 15 V. Technical 2D diagram The diagram illustrates the selected ACS geometry, the existing support line, attachment elevations and the direction and magnitude of the selected load components. Red arrows identify the live-load components for the selected force-level situation. Blue or dark arrows identify other load components. Positive and negative signs follow the coordinate system shown in the diagram.

Page 10 of 15 VI. Check against the existing structure The optional capacity field provides a quick orientation by comparing the governing calculated column load against a user-entered allowable value. Enter the allowable column load supplied by the responsible structural engineer, then run the capacity check. The calculator reports whether the entered capacity is exceeded by the governing value. IMPORTANT A passing indication is not a structural verification. The comparison does not assess stability, combined actions, connections, anchors, local effects, fatigue, seismic effects or th e complete set of applicable load combinations.

Page 11 of 15 VII. Characteristic and factored values The approved load tables contain characteristic preliminary values. Where the interface offers factored values, the displayed factors are an orientation based on the selected regional dataset. For the metric EU workflow, the interface may present the commonly used factors 1.35 for dead load and 1.50 for live load. For the USA workflow, the paired factors are 1.20 and 1.60. The responsible engineer must confirm the governing standard, load combinations and project-specific factors. IMPORTANT Never treat the optional factored display as a substitute for the structural design load combinations required for the project. Ambiguous signs Some load entries may contain positive and negative alternatives because different climbing-surface geometries with the same nominal input can produce different governing directions. The designer shall evaluate the unfavourable sign for the investigated structural system.

Page 12 of 15 VIII. Standard attachment details The attachment configurator helps the user browse standard details after choosing the supporting slab and the attachment method. The available choices are filtered by the selected ACS type and support category. The user may select details for a solid concrete slab or hollow-panel slab and review applicable support categories such as a concrete wall or column, steel column, and - where available - masonry wall. IMPORTANT The configurator does not size anchors or verify the resistance of a connection. Every selected detail must be checked for the actual substrate, geometry, loads and applicable standard.

Page 13 of 15 IX. Saving projects and exporting reports Signed-in users can save a calculation as a project, add tags and custom properties, search the project dashboard, reopen a previous calculation and save an updated copy. The PDF export records the selected inputs, calculated preliminary loads, key notes and technical diagrams. Store the report together with the project revision used for the structural review. IMPORTANT Before issuing a report, confirm the units, ACS type, height, attachment scheme, span A, overhang X and force level. A PDF only records the selected calculation state; it does not validate the input data. Recommended project record • Project name and revision. • Building and location. • Selected ACS geometry and supporting frame. • Calculation date and responsible user. • All force-level situations reviewed. • Exported PDF and any Engineering Support correspondence.

Page 14 of 15 X. Engineering Support and mobile use A saved project can be linked to a technical inquiry. The Engineering Support form includes the project calculation summary so the reviewing engineer can identify the selected geometry and load case. Describe the existing structure, the issue requiring review and the exact decision or clarification needed. Responses are sent by email. On mobile devices the same calculation inputs and results are presented in a vertical layout. Review the Results, Diagram and Notes sections before saving or exporting the project.

Page 15 of 15 XI. Final calculation checklist Before using the preliminary loads in an engineering assessment, confirm all items below: • Correct metric or imperial unit system selected. • Correct structure type selected: climbing wall or bouldering wall. • Wall height and attachment scheme match the project geometry. • Column span A represents the investigated existing frame. • Overhang X represents the local or most unfavourable geometry. • Every applicable live-load force level has been reviewed separately. • Signs and coordinate directions have been interpreted correctly. • Characteristic values have been factored according to the governing standard. • Special conditions at end and corner columns have been considered. • Attachment details and anchors will be verified by a qualified engineer. • The exported report is marked PRELIMINARY LOADS - NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION. IMPORTANT For anything beyond preliminary sizing or where the input geometry is outside the calculator dataset, contact Walltopia Engineering Support.
